PLPC is a lower-attention small-cap second-order candidate for grid electrical hardware, especially transmission, distribution and substation fittings; it needs deeper verification of Energy segment acceleration and utility capex linkage.
ETN remains the reference leader for backlog/order validation, but its mega-cap status means it should be used mainly as a pricing and demand signal rather than crowding out smaller suppliers.

Need a later pass for transformer-specific public exposure, including non-US ADRs/OTC names, transformer components, specialty steel/copper inputs, insulation fluids, testing/certification and utility substation automation suppliers.

POWL should be retained as a high-priority underfollowed grid-electrical-hardware candidate because it has direct medium-voltage switchgear/electrical distribution exposure and explicit fiscal 2026 backlog evidence tied to data centers, AI capacity growth, and electric utility demand.

MYRG should be retained as a second-order infrastructure-provider candidate for the same node; the key verification path is backlog mix by utility T&D, substation, data-center, and commercial/industrial electrical construction.
ETN remains the reference leader for market-pricing and demand validation, but should not dominate the underfollowed discovery lane because it is already a high-attention mega-cap.

Further Layer 1B searches should look for US-listed niche suppliers in transformer components, reclosers, relays, busway, cable accessories, substation automation, testing/inspection, and electrical distributors; likely candidates may be hidden under industrial-components or construction-services labels.

Add POWL as a priority underfollowed candidate for grid_electrical_hardware because its product list maps directly to switchgear, medium-voltage breakers, bus duct, packaged substations, and data-center / utility electrical systems; verify whether backlog is broad-based or mega-order concentrated.

Add PLPC as a low-attention second-order candidate for grid_electrical_hardware because it supplies transmission/distribution hardware, substation connectors/fittings, OPGW/ADSS monitoring-control network products, and has expanded HV/EHV substation connector exposure via acquisitions.

Testing, commissioning, relay/protection engineering, and substation field-services vendors appear highly relevant but many strong examples such as Qualus are private after the Clearlake acquisition; later passes should screen public engineering/testing/service substitutes and electrical contractors separately.

POWL should be carried forward as a direct underfollowed electrical-hardware candidate for data center and utility grid demand; key survival tests are backlog quality, margin durability, customer concentration, and manufacturing capacity.
HUBB should be treated primarily as a reference/context anchor for utility grid, substation, transmission, and grid-protection exposure rather than the main underfollowed alpha target.

IESC is a second-order underfollowed hypothesis: electrical installation/project execution may become a chokepoint adjacent to physical hardware, but data-center power exposure and backlog mix need verification.

Need a separate targeted pass for busway, cable accessories, reclosers, protection relays, and substation automation names that may be buried inside broader industrial or electronics classifications.
